page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not contain any GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific compute tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 35.44 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 202.24 GB/sec, both ranking in the strong tier. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 2191.0 and a multi-core score of 17995.0, with text processing reaching a top-tier score of 2884.0. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server demonstrated strong prompt processing at 2367.91 tokens/sec and top-tier text generation at 346.08 tokens/sec. However, memory-bound operations, such as large-block uncached memory writes at 63.7 GB/sec and Passmark database operations at 15634.59, remained in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32lds_v7 offers a high-density compute profile with dedicated CPU resources and fast local NVMe storage, making it a cost-effective choice for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff, limiting its suitability for large in-memory databases. This server is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
